title: Tech Note: Mirroring with 4D Server v11 SQL
author: Atanas Atanassov, Technical Services Team Member, 4D Inc.
featured_technology: SOAP web services (used for mirror configuration/entry points)

historical_commentary.text: This note introduced 4D v11 SQL's log-file-based database mirroring component, letting a mirror server stay continuously synchronized with a principal server for high availability without blocking the operational database for backups — a genuinely important capability for always-on deployments like hospitals or emergency services. The high-availability mirroring concept itself remains valid and 4D has continued to develop native mirroring/replication capabilities in subsequent versions, but the specific SOAP-based component and entry-point mechanism shown here reflects 4D's pre-REST web services era and would today more likely be built on 4D's newer, more integrated replication/mirroring features or a REST-based control layer rather than hand-rolled SOAP web services.
related_updates: 4D has continued to develop and refine native database mirroring/replication capabilities in later versions, reducing the need for a custom SOAP-based mirroring component
REST + ORDA (4D v16 R5+, 2017) has largely superseded SOAP as 4D's recommended way to expose and control services like this from external tools
